title: Providence controversy: unhappy calumny shared with Rome and the Remonstrants
pass_a_gloss: There returns not so much any true Controversy, as an unhappy Calumny of some, already common to these with the Pontiff & the Remonstrants. See the πρῶτα ψεύδη at length above at the Controversy with the Remonstrants VII, XV, XVIII, XIX, XXII.
pass_b_english: What comes back is not so much any true Controversy as an unhappy Calumny of a few — already shared by these men with the Papal party and with the Remonstrants. See the first falsehoods (πρῶτα ψεύδη) treated at length above in the Controversy with the Remonstrants, heads VII, XV, XVIII, XIX, and XXII.
source_text: Redit non tàm vera aliqua Controversia, quam infelix nonnullorum Calumnia, communis jam istis cum Pontif. & Remonstrantibus. Vide πρῶτα ψεύδη prolixè suprâ ad Controvers. cum Remonstr. VII. XV. XVIII. XIX. XXII.
notes: Short hinge paragraph before the phrase-catalogue that offended.

choices.why: Cross-ref to prior Remonstrant block; keep Greek and gloss
